description: Adversarial vectors for the permit decision-binding surface (claim permit.decision.v1). Each record derives from a published golden vector by applying the listed mutations, then adjudicating the result. Positive coverage lives in permit_decision_binding_golden_vectors_v1_v7.json; this file is the refusal half, so a third party can watch the binding fail as well as pass. The canonical_payload schema is closed (unknown signed fields are refused); the envelope is deliberately open, and envelope fields that restate signed values must agree with them.

verdict_tiers.supported: the binding is intact and trusted; this claim covers the signed canonical_payload, not unknown or unprotected envelope metadata
verdict_tiers.disproved: the artifact is affirmatively bad — tampered, forged, or malformed
verdict_tiers.insufficient_evidence: the verifier cannot decide because trust material is missing; NOT a statement that the artifact is bad
verdict_tiers.unverifiable_scope: the artifact is outside what this verifier version can adjudicate

trust_root_modes.all_published_keys: trust root contains binding_public_key plus every additional_binding_public_keys entry
trust_root_modes.empty: trust root present but with an empty key list
trust_root_modes.absent: trust root path that does not exist

mutation_ops.recompute_binding_hash: recompute artifact.binding_canonical_hash from the mutated canonical_payload, using canonical_binding_bytes for the artifact's binding_version
mutation_ops.copy_field_from_vector: overwrite `path` with the same field from the first golden vector whose binding_version equals `from_binding_version`
mutation_ops.flip_signature_byte: XOR 0xFF into byte `index` of the base64-decoded ed25519 signature

records.note: Control. If this record fails, the harness itself is wrong and every refusal below is uninterpretable.
Raise the signed spend ceiling after issuance and leave hash and signature untouched. The material parameter no longer recomputes to the signed hash.
Flip the adjudicated decision itself.
Expiry is covered by the signature, so backdating it is caught as tampering. This surface adjudicates binding integrity, not TTL policy.
The stronger attack: an adversary who understands the canonicalization recomputes the hash. The signature still covers the original hash, so forging the payload requires the signing key.
Same attack against the decision field, caught by payload cross-checks before signature verification is reached.
Single-bit corruption of the signature.
Signature substitution: a genuine signature, issued by a trusted key, over a different permit. Valid-but-unrelated evidence must not transfer.
Intact artifact signed by a key absent from the trust root. Distinct from disproved: the verifier is not asserting the permit is bad, only that it cannot vouch for the signer.
Trust root present but carrying no keys.
No trust material at all. A relying party must map this to refuse-the-consequential-effect; it is not a pass, and it is not proof of tampering.
A binding version this verifier build cannot canonicalize. Reported as out-of-scope rather than as a failure, so an old verifier cannot silently condemn a newer artifact.
Evidence stripped of its signature must not degrade into an unsigned pass.

The unsigned envelope copy of binding_version contradicts the signed one. Nothing about the signature is wrong; the artifact is internally inconsistent, and a consumer reading the envelope would see a value the signature does not cover.

Envelope key id relabelled to a different trusted key. Key resolution uses the signed copy, so verification still succeeds; the mismatch is refused so a report cannot attribute the signature to the wrong key.
Pre-existing instance of the same invariant, pinned here so the three envelope/payload agreement checks are documented together.
The signed copy is covered by the hash, so altering it is ordinary tampering rather than an envelope inconsistency.

Both copies moved together so the consistency check passes, but the artifact was never re-signed and a v5 binding requires evidence a v1 artifact does not carry. Version confusion cannot be laundered by editing both copies.
The signed payload schema is closed: an unrecognised signed field is refused rather than ignored.

DELIBERATE NON-CLAIM, pinned so the decision stays explicit. The envelope is open, and a supported verdict says nothing about unknown envelope metadata: it covers the signed canonical_payload only. Anything presenting this artifact must not display unrecognised envelope fields as verified. If the envelope is ever closed, this record must change with it.

Pins the precedence: the envelope-consistency check runs BEFORE signature verification, so an artifact that is both inconsistent and forged reports the inconsistency. A CANONICAL_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH verdict therefore says nothing about whether the signature was valid — the claim's epistemic_state records only that envelope and payload disagree.
